quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
School zone.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows a crosswalk. Watch for people crossing the road.

questions.question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.
Follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, stay calm and focus on the road. Don't get upset by other drivers. Leave extra time for your trip, follow the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or damage property, you must leave a note. Write your name, phone number, and address. Attach it securely to the vehicle you hit.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers may try to pass before you do.
Because following too closely will affect your vehicle's performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see better around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of large trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles with trailers cannot see you if you are directly behind them. Stay farther back. This also helps you see the road ahead around the large vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before it catches up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches from any direction with flashing red or blue lights, pull to the right side of the road and stop. Do not try to drive faster than the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if the road is wet or icy?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires cannot grip the road as well as they do on dry roads. You must slow down.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when pulling up to a curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: You exit a freeway on a downhill curved ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the curve.
Slow down to the freeway speed limit.
Start braking after you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Your vehicle has a mechanical problem. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down, turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you. Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic if possible.

questions.question: When driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it is dark and hard to see. Use headlights properly, switching between high and low beams as needed. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as this can blind you.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you do?

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads are slippery. Your tires do not grip the road as well as they do on pavement. You must slow down. It will take longer to stop and you can skid more easily when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead.
Merge traffic.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming up ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Cross the centerline at an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline at an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never pass or change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other drivers. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with flashing lights and a stop arm, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when the children finish exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when a school bus has its stop arm out and lights flashing. Stay stopped until the stop arm goes in and the lights turn off.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let traffic that could cause a conflict pass first.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let traffic that could cause a conflict pass first.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop. You can go if there is no other traffic coming.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only the side with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs are safe for driving if you take the right dose.
All medicines prescribed by a doctor are safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medicines can make you drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medicines—prescription and over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines often make you drowsy. You must know how your medicine affects you before you drive.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Walk all the way around your vehicle to check for people or objects.
Rev your engine.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk all the way around your vehicle to check for people or objects.
questions.explanation: Walk around your entire vehicle before backing up. Look over your shoulder and out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes quickly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes quickly without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes. Use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Check for vehicles behind and beside you. Never change lanes suddenly.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when can you safely move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the car over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: When a school bus picks up or drops off children, you must:

options.text: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
Stop only if you are driving the same direction.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, no matter which direction you are driving.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop before reaching a school bus that is picking up or dropping off children. This applies whether you are driving toward it or in the same direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Falling rocks
Trucks use second gear
Steep hill

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign means a steep hill is coming. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
Drink something with caffeine.
Open a window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Take a break every hour on long trips. Share driving with another person so you can both rest safely.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Annoy drivers about traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests to guide you safely through.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and go only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look both ways before going through. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than cars. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use:

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see.

questions.question: If your car's rear end skids to the left, you should:

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want the front to go. If the rear skids left, steer left to straighten the car.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and go only when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see both directions clearly.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. When the gate is raised, only cross if you can see clearly in both directions and are sure no train is coming.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: You can pass from both directions.
You can pass only in your direction.
No one can pass in either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass in either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. You must:

options.text: Slow down because a lane is ending.
Watch for workers and equipment.
Change lanes and keep your speed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for workers and equipment.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean it is loading or unloading students. Do not go until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes up. Never pass a school bus picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Keep your engine warm.
Help others see your vehicle.
Warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help others see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have trouble seeing you. Headlights make your vehicle easier to spot. If you turn on wipers, turn on your low beam headlights too.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Tap or pump the brakes.
Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
Apply the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and brake lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas and slow down. Do not use the brakes until the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: What do blue traffic signs tell you about?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Distance to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs give information about services for drivers, such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Intersection ahead.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to situations ahead. This sign warns of an upcoming intersection so you can prepare to stop or turn.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to turn before the light changes.
You don't need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic pass before turning.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:

options.text: Left, then right, then left again.
Right.
Left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from the left will reach you faster than vehicles from the right. Check that the path is clear before you move.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must drive through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The top speed you can drive is 55 mph under good conditions.
You must not drive below the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The top speed you can drive is 55 mph under good conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the maximum speed limit for that road. You may drive slower than the posted limit based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: If you are driving on a highway next to a single broken white line:

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: At a red light, if a police officer tells you to go through the intersection without stopping, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer directing traffic has authority over traffic signals and signs. Always follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of roads with two-way traffic. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A dashed yellow line means you may cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: The roadway center has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You are not allowed to pass in this area.
You may pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is on your side of the road center, you are in a passing zone. You may pass safely when no oncoming traffic is present.

questions.question: Construction and maintenance work zones use traffic control devices that are:

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange warning signs on the road.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass a car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on the shoulder. The driver ahead will not expect you to be there and may pull onto the shoulder. You can only pass on the right if you stay on the roadway.

questions.question: When you drive through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive carefully through and do not slow down to look at things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through and do not slow down to look at things.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things on the road. This is called "rubbernecking" and causes traffic jams. Drive through construction zones carefully without stopping to watch.

questions.question: If you park your vehicle in an unusual location, you should:

options.text: Park with your reverse lights on.
Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
Park five feet from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see your vehicle from all directions.
questions.explanation: Your parked car must not become a hazard. Make sure drivers approaching from any direction can see your vehicle clearly.
